The size of the video. Original keeps the picture\'s own size; the others fit inside that box without cropping or stretching.

The encoder may refuse or lower a value above its listed maximum. If it refuses, the export retries once at the maximum.

Sets how loud the exported audio is. Off keeps the clip exactly as it is. The others normalize to the target level and keep the true peak under −1 dBTP.

10-bit needs the original size, no crop or straighten, a grade the GPU path supports and a 10-bit encoder. Here it is not available, so the file will be 8-bit.
%1$s is not available yet. The file will be SDR.
The encoder does not offer %1$s. The export will use %2$s.

%1$s Mbps is above the encoder\'s listed maximum of %2$s Mbps. The encoder may refuse or lower it.
%1$s Mbps is below the encoder\'s minimum. It is raised to %2$s Mbps.
The encoder does not offer that profile. Auto is used.
%1$s is a software encoder. Expect a slow export.
Compatible plays everywhere (H.264). Smaller uses HEVC at a low bitrate. Quality uses HEVC at the highest level. Changing any setting makes it Custom.
H.264 plays on almost every device. HEVC makes smaller files at the same quality but needs a newer player.
Megabits per second of video. The levels scale with the picture size and frame rate. Higher means a bigger file and fewer compression artifacts.
Variable (VBR) spends bits where the picture needs them. Constant (CBR) keeps the rate steady, which some players and uploads prefer.
How often a full picture is stored. Shorter is easier to edit and seek, longer is smaller. Every frame is the largest and the easiest to edit.
Auto lets the encoder choose. Pick one only if a player needs it.
Audio quality of the AAC track. The sample rate and channel count follow the clip.
10-bit needs the original size, no crop or straighten, a grade the GPU path supports and a 10-bit encoder. It is made on the GPU path only.
10-bit (HEVC Main10) keeps smooth gradients like skies without banding. It is rendered on the GPU path at the original size. Players need to support 10-bit HEVC.
10-bit was asked for but not available for this export. The file is 8-bit.
The finished file could not be found or opened. Recovery: export the clip again.
No app on this device can open a raw DNG. Share the file to a reader that can.

Playback and scrubbing resolution. Lower is smoother playback; paused frames always sharpen to the clip\'s own resolution.

Where the develop pipeline runs. CPU is the reference path; Auto uses the GPU when this device verifies it; GPU is experimental and falls back to CPU when unavailable. The video encoder is chosen separately and is not affected by this setting.
Follow the system theme, or pin the app to light or dark. The editor screens keep their fixed neutral look either way.
